findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a staff member wash their hands, then fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was provided. Ensure the use of a barrier after completing hand washing to prevent re-contaminating hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ground beef at 119F. CORRECTED- it was verified that the food had been in the unit less than 4 hours, and the unit was turned from “1” to “3”. Food was then observed to have an internal temperature of 140F. Ensure hot holding units are always set so that hot temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods have an internal temperature of 135F or higher.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed TCS foods in the standing cooler (nearest the door) to have internal temperatures between 45-50 (hotdogs and hamburgers respectively). CORRECTED- items that had been in the unit less than 4 hours were moved to a working cooler or implemented under time as control (items are to be used or discarded within 4 hours). Items housed in the unit over 4 hours were discarded. Ensure all TCS foods (including all animal proteins, house made products using mayo as an ingredient, cut tomatoes, and shredded lettuce) are cold held at or below 41F, or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the standing cooler nearest to door to have an ambient temperature of 50F, and failing to hold TCS items at or below 41F (see violation #22). A follow up is being scheduled for 6/26/26 to verify compliance. Ensure the unit has been serviced to cold hold foods below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/CFPM) on staff does not have Allergen Awareness training. Inspector provided Allergen Awareness training information to the PIC. Ensure all CFMs obtain Allergen Awareness training, to be maintained on file every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to produce their Certified Food Manager (CFM/ CFPM) certificate during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- a CFM arrived on site. Ensure a CFM is present on site at all times food is being cooked or prepared, and maintain files on site for future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen to contain soap, and no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was remade to display 200 ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made with ONLY warm water and a chemical sanitizer, as soap interferes with sanitizing ability of chemical.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled white powder in the kitchen. CORRECTED- a kitchen staff member labeled the product as sugar. Ensure any ready to eat (RTE) food products that may be easily mistaken for another is labeled once removed from its original container to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces where observed to be in need of repair or reconditioning:
1) The gaskets at BOTH standing coolers and the standing freezer in the kitchen are fragmenting.
2) One of the microwave handles is loose from the door.
3) Some shelves in the standing cooler directly next to the fryers are rusted. Clean/ reseal/ paint, or replace rusting shelves.
Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are in proper repair to prevent potential contamination of foods. Nonfoodcontact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.[C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The only Allergen certificates available were observed to have been expired. Inspector provided Allergen Awareness training information to the PIC. Ensure CFMs obtain Allergen Awareness training, to be maintained every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee washing their hands. Upon completion of hand washing, the employee turned off the faucet with a bare hand. Inspector talked with the employee, as well as the PIC about hand washing procedures. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after washing hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build-up of soils on the soda nozzles of the soda machine. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that soda nozzles are cleaned regularly enough to keep soils from depositing. Inspector will return 07/28/2025 to re-inspect the condition of the soda nozzles.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility to not have any quat test strips. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the proper test strips are kept in the facility at all times. Inspector will return 07/28/2025 to check and see if test strips have been acquired.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no date marks on juices being used in bar coolers. Discussed date marking procedures with PIC. PIC added date marks to the open juices in the cooler. Ensure all opened TCS foods are date-marked upon opening.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Ice machine contained mold and mildew on baffles.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on site.  Ensure ice machine is cleaned regularly to prevent contamination of ice.

4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The sanitizer bucket at the bar had a concentration of 0 ppm (q) and the kitchen had just dumped the bucket from lunch and had not refilled at time of inspection.  Discussed with employees, who changed and filled the sanitizer buckets. Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed and refilled regularly to properly sanitize surfaces.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Ice machine contained mold and mildew on baffles.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on site.  Ensure ice machine is cleaned regularly to prevent contamination of ice.

4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Ice scoop was observed to be stored in the ice in the ice machine, with the handle in contact with the ice.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on site.  Ensure ice scoop is stored in the ice scoop holder to prevent contamination of ice.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed food container lids stored in a clear plastic bin which contained food debris.  Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch.  Ensure storage bin is covered to prevent food and dust debris from contaminating food contact surfaces.  

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Window air-conditioning unit was observed to contain a build-up of dust residue.  Air-conditioning unit is located above food prep counter.  Ensure air-conditioner is frequently cleaned to prevent the build-up of dust residue and contamination of foods.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a wooden block on prep counter.  PIC stated it is used to prevent the food slicer from coming in contact with the wall behind, causing paint/wall chipping.  Inspector advised PIC wood block is required to be painted or sealed to create a smooth, non-absorbent, easily cleanable surface.  Ensure block is treated to obtain a non-absorbent surface.

Inspector observed a paint chip above the 3-part sink.  Ensure to apply a layer of paint as to create a smooth, non-absorbent, easily cleanable surface.  

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C)

There is no thermometer in white fridge in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC. Ensure thermometers are kept in refrigerator units at all times, especially when cooling to monitor overall temp in fridge. COS- thermometer placed in fridge, after about 25 minutes, thermometers reads 40 degrees. Keep extras on hand to replace when necessary.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. 

Small gap present in back door to kitchen along the floor. Discussed with PIC. Door is going to be replaced in the near future. Ensure door frame is solid and flush to the frame, so no gaps visible to protect against entry of pests and rodents.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

Observed cardboard being used as a tray to hold individually portioned cups of sauces and dressings. Discussed with PIC. Cease use of cardboard in the kitchen and bar areas. All materials in contact with food products must be smooth and easily cleanable items. COS- Staff switched out cardboard for smooth plastic Tupperware.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Plumbing appears to have been shifted underneath the 3-part sink. Holes in wall present where old piping used to be. See that holes are sealed with plaster and painted to render wall smooth and easily cleanable by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

A wooden pallet observed used to prop up a cooler in the bar area. Ensure pallet is either stained or painted to be rendered smooth and easily cleanable by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. 
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only. 

While assisting inspector with inspection of fridge, employee lightly rinsed their hands in the middle of the 3-part sink and shut off faucet with hands. Inspector then advised employee that handwashing should only occur in handwashing sink. Employee then went to hand sink, pumped soap into hands, 3-4 seconds of washing, and then shut off the faucet with bare hands, then dried off hands on cloth rags used in food prep in kitchen. Inspector advised proper handwashing technique includes a 20-second wash, drying hands with a disposable paper towel, and using towel to shut off faucet. Employee rewashed hands for an acceptable time, then used bare hands to shut off faucet again. About a minute or two later, employee then rinsed hands under 3-part sink for a second time. Discussed need to re-train employees on proper handwashing techniques as numerous violations were observed during inspection.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands – except washing fruits and veggies (P). 

Upon entry to the kitchen for an inspection, inspector observed employee slicing tomatoes and green bell peppers with bare hands. When inspector inquired about the use of these food items, the employee replied they were to be toppings on sandwiches. Inspector advised employee that gloves should be worn when handling ready to eat foods. Employee donned gloves.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). 

Raw shell eggs stored above RTE sauce containers in white fridge in kitchen. Ensure raw eggs, raw meat are stored below RTE foods so a spill does not contaminate RTE foods. Eggs were moved to a lower shelf.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) 

Cheese sauce was heating in a hot holding unit, probed at 53 degrees. Inspector asked employee how long it had been there, they stated about 10 minutes. Employee was unable to tell inspector proper hot holding temperature for cheese sauce. Discussed with PIC reheating practices. Hot holding units, unless specified by the manufacturer, are meant to keep hot food hot, not make cold food hot. TCS foods should be cooked on either stovetop or oven to appropriate temperatures (mentioned above) prior to being placed in hot holding unit. Cheese was moved to a stovetop for a rapid heat.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C)

There is no thermometer in white fridge in the kitchen. Provide a thermometer in this unit by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

REPEAT- CFMs do not have proof of allergen awareness certification. Provide proof by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A) Thermometer in the prepped food fridge was reading 51 degrees. Employees were recently in and out of the fridge prepping. All foods in the fridge temped below 41 degrees except for 2 small containers of cheese sauce. Containers of cheese sauce were probed at 47 and 48. Cheese sauces were voluntarily discarded at time of inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07. Allergen awareness training.
(b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic.

Facility has chlorine test strips on hand, but no quaternary ammonium test strips. PIC will purchase new strips today.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The present manager is not a certified food manager. The food handler card is present.  The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Raw eggs are observed stored above ready-to-eat veggies and prepared foods. Store below ready-to-eat foodsso they are separate and protected against cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Multiple frozen foods are thawing at room temperature (pork patties, beef patties, soups). Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed no thermometer in the pizza reach-in freezer. Provide a thermometer in the pizza reach-in freezer. A thermometer was provided in the pizza reach-in freezer during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-230 A calibrate metal-stemmed thermometer accurate to ±2F° shall be provided for checking temperatures on food.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a wet wiping cloth laying on the counter near the hand sink in the bar area. Store all wet wiping cloths in a properly sanitized bucket when not in use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the microwave near the reach-in freezer to be soiled. Clean the microwave near the reach-in freezer.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed no FSSMC during the arrival of the inspector. Provide a FSSMC during all shifts the facility is open. The FSSMC arrived during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed the ice scoop handle in contact with the ice in the cooler behind the bar. Store the ice scooper with the handle extending out of the ice. The ice scooper was stored properly during the routine inspection to correct the violation.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed single service containers to be stored with the food contact surface exposed. Store all single service items in a manner of protecting the food contact surface. The single service containers were properly stored during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a container of chicken salad in the refrigerator with no label. Provide a label on the chicken salad in the refrigerator. A label was provided on the chicken salad in the refrigerator during the routine inspection to correct the violation.
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a gallon of milk in the reach-in cooler with no date mark. The manager stated it was opened Sunday. Provide a date mark on the milk in the reach-in cooler. A date mark of 03/19 Sunday's date was provided on the gallon of milk in the reach-in cooler to, during the routine inspection to correct the violation.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a bulk container of barbcue sauce stored under the grill area. The barbecue sauce should be stored in the refrigerator after opening. The barbcue sauce was discarded during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
•Observed no (Cl-) test strips in the facility. Provide cholorine test strips in the facility.
750-830c A thermometer ±3°F shall be provided to check the temperature of  the water in each tank of the dish machine and the temperature of  the final rinse water as it enters the manifold.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed single service paper towel and toliet tissue on the floor in the back storage room. Store all single service items at least six inches off the floor. The paper towels and toliet tissue were place on the bottom rack in the storage room during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
